documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Regional hospital emergency department. Visit 02/10/2026, arrived 21:40.

CC: roommate concerned about odd behavior.

HPI: 23-year-old woman brought in by her roommate. For the past several weeks she has kept to her room and rarely comes out. She tells us she believes her thoughts are going out over the radio where other people can hear them, and that she hears voices that talk about what she is doing. Patient is guarded and answers briefly; roommate supplies most of the history. No prior psychiatric diagnosis or treatment. Denies drug use.

PMH: seasonal allergic rhinitis, acne.
PSH: tonsillectomy as a child; wisdom teeth extraction.
Home meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily; clindamycin 1% gel to face twice daily.
Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.
Family history: no family psychiatric history obtained at this visit.
Social: never smoker, alcohol on weekends, 1-2 drinks. College student, works part time at a coffee shop.

Vitals: within normal limits, see flowsheet.
Exam: Unkempt hair and clothing. Appears to be attending to internal stimuli, glancing to the side and pausing mid-answer. Alert and oriented x3. Recall intact. Speech coherent, slowed and soft. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams unremarkable.

Results: CBC normal. BMP normal. TSH normal. Urine toxicology negative.

Assessment: new-onset psychotic symptoms with thought broadcasting and auditory hallucinations; medical and substance causes not supported by today's workup. Schizophreniform disorder.

Disposition: discharged home in the care of her roommate. Outpatient psychiatry referral information provided. No medications started. Return for any thoughts of harming self or others or worsening symptoms.

Record received by fax 02/13/2026.

OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Regional hospital ED. Date of service 03/21/2026.

CC: behavior getting worse; not going to school or work.

HPI: 23F with allergic rhinitis and acne, seen here about a month ago for new psychotic symptoms. Brought back today by the same roommate. Since then she has pulled away further and is often heard talking to herself. She has told the roommate that the government put a chip in her brain. She stopped going to her classes and recently quit her coffee shop job, convinced her coworkers were in on a plan to keep watch on her. This is her first psychiatric illness; she has not connected with outpatient psychiatry.

Problems: schizophreniform disorder (this ED, 02/2026); seasonal allergic rhinitis; acne vulgaris.
PSH: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth.
Home meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily; clindamycin 1% gel BID.
Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.
FH: maternal uncle with schizophrenia; paternal grandmother with bipolar I; mother with generalized anxiety disorder.
Social: never smoker; weekend alcohol 1-2 drinks.

MSE: disheveled, visibly anxious, looks away throughout. Preoccupied, mumbles under her breath while being interviewed. Speech disorganized. Expresses fixed paranoid beliefs about being monitored.

Results: urine toxicology negative.

Impression: schizophreniform disorder, worsening.
Disposition: discharged home with roommate; outpatient psychiatry referral renewed with contact numbers. No medications started.

Received by fax 03/25/2026.

OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Regional hospital ED, 05/23/2026.

CC: increasingly unusual behavior.

HPI: 23-year-old woman, third ED visit since February for progressive psychotic symptoms (social withdrawal, thought broadcasting, hearing voices, persecutory beliefs). Roommate brought her in. Over roughly three months she has become more isolated and mutters to herself in her room for hours. She let her work responsibilities slide and then stopped going in at all. Roommate describes laughing at odd moments and reacting to things no one else sees. It is hard to hold a conversation with her; she skips from one unrelated subject to another. She has stopped showering, and her hair and clothes are unwashed.

Problems: schizophreniform disorder; seasonal allergic rhinitis; acne vulgaris.
Home meds (as reported): cetirizine, drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol, clindamycin gel.
Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.
FH: maternal uncle schizophrenia; paternal grandmother bipolar I; mother GAD.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks on weekends.

Exam: minimal eye contact, flat affect, speech mumbled with loose associations. Neuro: cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation normal, gait steady; nonfocal.

Results: urine drug screen negative. BMP within normal limits.

Impression: schizophreniform disorder, progressive.
Disposition: discharged home with roommate. Outpatient psychiatry intake appointment arranged for early June. No medications started.

Received 05/27/2026.

documents.title: Psychiatry Initial Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY
Initial evaluation, seen 06/09/2026.

Reason for referral: first-episode psychosis after three ED visits (February, March and May 2026).

History: 23-year-old woman, undergraduate biology student, until this winter also working part time as a barista; she has stopped attending classes. Over the past several months she has withdrawn from friends, stopped working and spends most of the day in her room. She endorses hearing voices that remark on what she does and a belief that others can hear her thoughts; she still feels she is being watched. Workup in the ED, including blood counts, chemistries, TSH and repeated urine drug screens, was unrevealing. No prior psychiatric treatment. Denies substance use; weekend alcohol only, never smoker. Lives with her roommate; her mother came to today's appointment and is involved.

Family psychiatric history: maternal uncle with schizophrenia; paternal grandmother with bipolar I disorder; mother with generalized anxiety disorder.

Medical: seasonal allergic rhinitis, acne. Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily, drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily, clindamycin 1% gel. Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.

MSE: poorly groomed, limited eye contact, flat affect, speech soft with tangential stretches, perceptual disturbances endorsed, persecutory content, no suicidal or homicidal ideation, insight limited.

Diagnosis: schizophreniform disorder.

Plan:
1. Start aripiprazole 5 mg by mouth once daily. Reviewed common side effects including restlessness, and the reason for an antipsychotic. Patient and mother agree.
2. Weight and metabolic monitoring will be followed here.
3. Return in 6 weeks, sooner if worse. Crisis line numbers given.

Please contact our office with any concerns. cc: primary care physician.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY
Follow-up, seen 07/21/2026.

Yolanda returns six weeks after starting aripiprazole 5 mg daily, with her mother. Taking it every evening; her mother has been helping her keep track. Voices come less often now and bother her less when they do. No restlessness, no stiffness or tremor. Weight unchanged from the first visit.

MSE: casually dressed, better groomed than at intake, eye contact improved but still brief, affect restricted, speech more organized, no suicidal ideation.

Assessment: schizophreniform disorder, partial response to aripiprazole, tolerating well.
Plan: continue aripiprazole 5 mg daily. Return in about 6 weeks.

cc: primary care physician.
